Derived from date of birth (item 1, complete for every respondent) and an assumed collection date of 2022-03-31, the midpoint of the January-June 2022 window established under data_year. Mean 15.99 years, range 13.3 to 22.2. Residual uncertainty from the unknown collection date is about plus or minus 0.25 years. Do NOT use the EDAD column: it is the volatile worksheet formula YEAR(TODAY()) - YEAR(birth date) and holds ages at the workbook's last recalculation, giving an implausible 18-26. The source papers report calendar-year age (2022 minus birth year, M = 16.19), which runs about 0.3 years higher than the age recorded here because it is age at the end of 2022. 23 respondents exceed the schema maximum of 19 and 6 are 20 or older; their true ages are kept rather than set to missing, so that the project can apply its own age eligibility rule.

Item 7, '¿Aproximadamente cuántas horas diarias dedicas a las Redes sociales (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, etc)?', weekday column. Content-based and independent of any device item, as the schema requires. Five-option ordinal band scale shared by items 7 and 8, scored at band midpoints: 1 'menos de 1 hora' = 0.5, 2 'entre 1 y 3 horas' = 2, 3 'entre 3 y 5 horas' = 4. The open top band 4 'más de 5 horas' is scored 6, i.e. as if it had the same width as the band below it, following the project convention used in BPIPD-170 and BPIPD-270. Option 5 'no uso redes sociales' is a non-use response rather than a higher band and is scored 0 hours. Caution: option 5 is inconsistent across the two days. 41 respondents report 1 or more hours of social media on weekdays yet choose 'no uso redes sociales' for the weekend (7 do the reverse, and 38 choose it for both days), and the weekend distribution is otherwise shifted upward, so some respondents appear to have read the last column as 'even more than 5 hours'. The weekend zeros are therefore less trustworthy than the weekday ones. Scoring option 5 as 0 rather than missing is a project decision, taken because it is the literal meaning of the option and preserves genuine non-users as true zeros. Harmonised mean 2.80 hours/day.

No time item for making or posting content. Items 15.1-15.10 ask how often the respondent performs prosocial acts through electronic media, which is a frequency, not a duration.

The study's SMASI-SO block (items 23.1-23.8) is the only candidate, and every item is conditioned on 'por mi orientación sexual o identidad de género' - being mocked (23.6) or attacked (23.7) on social media because of sexual orientation or gender identity. Dichotomising it would make TRUE valid but FALSE wrong for anyone bullied online for any other reason, so it misclassifies rather than merely under-covers the construct. Project decision: leave unmapped rather than contribute a biased binary.
No perpetration item. The SMASI-SO block asks only about being targeted; see beh_beenbullied_online.

The study measures online prosocial behaviour with the Online Prosocial Behaviour Scale, which is mapped to beh_prosocial_online_self. That is not the SDQ prosocial subscale, is restricted to acts performed through electronic media, and cannot be scored onto this row; never pool the two.

Online Prosocial Behaviour Scale, emitted subscale: items 15.1-15.10 ask how often in the past month the respondent did each prosocial act 'a través de los medios electrónicos (teléfono móvil, portátil, tableta, etc.)', scored 1 nunca, 2 alguna vez al mes, 3 alguna vez a la semana, 4 varias veces a la semana, 5 todos los días. Summed with no reverse-scored items - all ten are positively worded - giving a 10-50 range. Observed range 10-50, mean 31.5, SD 8.7, Cronbach's alpha 0.893; complete for all 1,273 respondents, so the strict sum loses nobody. The parallel received subscale (items 16.1-16.10, alpha 0.920, complete for 1,239) is deliberately not mapped: it records prosocial acts others directed at the respondent, which is a different construct and has no dataschema row.

expression: "Online Prosocial Behaviour Scale, emitted subscale, 10 of 10 items, 1-5 item scoring (range 10-50), sum, past-month recall, no reverse-scored items"
notes: Constant for this single-occasion study; see beh_prosocial_online_self.
No loneliness item; the questionnaire has no mental-health block.

The study's only wellbeing instrument is the 21-item Questionnaire for Eudaimonic Well-Being, which is mapped to wb_eudaimonic_self. Eudaimonic wellbeing is not equivalent to the hedonic and functioning content of WEMWBS, SWEMWBS or WHO-5 and must not be pooled with them.

Questionnaire for Eudaimonic Well-Being (QEWB), items 18.1-18.21, scored 1 totalmente en desacuerdo to 6 totalmente de acuerdo. Summed as stored, giving a 21-126 range. Observed range 21-126, mean 77.3, SD 16.4, Cronbach's alpha 0.863; complete for all 1,273 respondents. IMPORTANT: the released data are already keyed so that a high value means high eudaimonic wellbeing, so the eight negatively worded items (18.3, 18.7, 18.10, 18.11, 18.12, 18.16, 18.19, 18.20) must NOT be reverse-scored again. Evidence: as stored, every item correlates positively with the rest of the scale (item-rest r 0.18 to 0.62) and alpha is 0.863, whereas reverse-scoring those eight turns three item-rest correlations negative (18.3 = -0.22, 18.7 = -0.08, 18.10 = -0.27) and drops alpha to 0.733. No document in the study folder states the scoring direction, so it is inferred from the data.
